transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Devin Park (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Zenith Head of AI), Tom Delaney (Zenith VP Eng), Sanjay Patel (Zenith Infra), Megan Liu (Zenith Procurement), Ana Gomez (Zenith DS)

Summary: POC scoping focused on commercial guardrails for a 4-6 week pilot: credits, pilot terms, success criteria, benchmarks, timeline, and path to procurement/contracting. Technical notes on workload sizing, representative prompts, latency/throughput targets, and private deployment constraints.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros? We'll run about 45-60 minutes, want to make sure we capture success criteria and commercial guardrails for the POC.
[00:12] Priya (Zenith): Hi, Priya here. We're trying to evaluate an LLM inference platform for clinical note summarization and triage routing. Key constraints: PHI, low latency, and integration with our VPC.
[00:26] Tom (Zenith): Tom—engineering—our rough ask is a pilot to validate latency and throughput at our daily volume, and a clear path to procurement if it meets criteria.
[00:38] Lena: Great. Marcus, can you frame the standard benchmark we propose?
[00:42] Marcus (Redwood): Yeah, typically for these pilots we do a 4-week benchmark. We'll run two phases: synthetic load to validate throughput and latency, and then a representative run using your 10k sample prompts for quality/regression checks. Key metrics: p50/p95 latency for 512-token requests, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression vs your baseline. For PHI we can discuss private deployment options—VPC or on-prem—depending on policy.
[01:10] Priya: Sounds good. For quality success, we need no more than 5% regression on our eval set vs current model, and p95 latency under 300ms for short responses (<=256 tokens). Is that realistic?
[01:25] Marcus: 300ms p95 is achievable on dedicated GPUs for that token length, we'll validate. For 512 tokens 300ms may be aggressive depending on model and quantization; we'll surface options with batching and KV cache profiles.
[01:40] Tom: On scale, our average is 200 RPS during peak and about 1.2M tokens/day on average. We need to know how many dedicated GPUs that maps to.
[01:52] Marcus: We'll size that in the cluster worksheet but as a rough rule, 8 A100-sized GPUs can handle X given moderate batching—I'll quantify after we see your token distribution.
[02:05] Lena: Let's move to commercial guardrails—what we normally provide for pilots is a credits package and pilot terms. Typical offering: 4-week pilot with $25k of credits applied to usage, optional extended pilot at a reduced rate. We also include a short SOW and SLAs during the pilot window.
[02:26] Megan (Zenith): Procurement here—what does $25k cover? Is that compute only? Any extra fees? Also need to know path to an enterprise contract.
[02:36] Lena: Credits cover platform usage (per-token inference and embeddings). They don't cover optional on-prem appliance hardware if you choose an air-gapped deployment—those would be separately quoted. For enterprise contracting, typical path: POC -> SOW/Statement of Work -> PO under standard MSA. We can share our MSA and security pack for review.
[02:54] Megan: Timeline? We have an internal target to finish procurement by end of Q4.
[03:00] Lena: If the pilot starts in early October, and results are positive, we can move to commercial talks and an SOW within 3-4 weeks after pilot close. Procurement review typically needs the MSA, SOC2 docs, and an SOW with pricing—we'll provide a redlineable SOW template.
[03:17] Ana (Zenith): For acceptance criteria, can we codify automated regression thresholds? We want to avoid subjective signoff.
[03:24] Marcus: Absolutely. We'll produce a success criteria spreadsheet: pass/fail thresholds for p95 latency, throughput, and NLU metrics (e.g., Rouge/accuracy on your eval set). We'll also include tokenized cost per inference targets.
[03:37] Priya: About data residency and PHI—we need KMS-based encryption and logs retained in our account; also SSO/SAML and RBAC for user access.
[03:47] Devin (Redwood): We support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for private deployments. For hosted pilots we can also sign a BAA and restrict logs. If you need on-prem, we'd coordinate an on-site package and give a separate quote.
[04:03] Sanjay (Zenith): Our infra team will need network diagrams and required ports—can you send an architecture doc?
[04:08] Marcus: Yes, we'll share a private deployment checklist and network diagram.
[04:12] Tom: Back to commercial guardrails—what happens if we hit the credits before pilot ends? Do we cut off, or move to pay-as-you-go?
[04:20] Lena: Two options: allow overage billing at the agreed pilot rate, or pause service until commercial agreement. We usually recommend overage billing to keep the pilot running; we'll include clear caps in the POC doc.
[04:31] Megan: For PO and invoicing, we need line-item pricing and a limit on exposure. We also prefer fixed-cost pilots where possible to stay within budget.
[04:40] Lena: We can structure the POC as fixed-value credits—e.g., $25k credit covers up to X throughput. If you prefer a fixed pilot fee, we can propose a flat pilot price that includes compute and Redwood support.
[04:52] Priya: Are there performance guarantees during the POC? We can't accept wildly variable latencies.
[04:58] Lena: During the pilot we offer operational SLOs for the dedicated pool (uptime and basic latency targets), but full SLA inclusion is typically in committed Dedicated contracts. For the pilot we commit to prioritizing your tests and giving remediation if baseline metrics are missed.
[05:12] Tom: Ok. Marcus, what's your benchmarking plan end-to-end so procurement can see reproducible steps?
[05:18] Marcus: Phase 1: synthetic load tests with step-up concurrency to establish throughput curves and resource utilization. Phase 2: representative quality run using your 10k prompt set and holdout eval. We'll run multiple seeds, compute p50/p95, token/sec, and compute cost per 1k tokens. We'll also run an A/B vs your current model to detect regressions.
[05:36] Ana: We'll provide the prompt set but need guidance on data masking for PHI.
[05:41] Devin: We'll accept a masked or synthetic set; Marcus will share a templated dataset format.
[05:46] Marcus: Also we'll log inference traces for debugging—those can be scrubbed or kept in your project.
[05:51] Priya: For acceptance, threshold examples: p95 latency <300ms for <=256 tokens, p95 <700ms for 512 tokens; regression <=5% on key recall metric. Also, cost per 1k tokens should be within 20% of our current cost baseline.
[06:08] Lena: Great, we'll codify those into the success spreadsheet.
[06:12] Megan: On contracting—if the pilot goes well, how long until enterprise pricing and commitment? We need at least 30 days to review T&Cs.
[06:20] Lena: After pilot close we typically run a commercial review; if you want Dedicated, we provide a proposal in 1-2 weeks with pricing tiers and reserved capacity options. Procurement cycle of 30-60 days is common.
[06:30] Tom: Any required security documents to start? We need SOC2 and pen test reports, and a data processing addendum.
[06:36] Lena: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, a security questionnaire, and a BAA if PHI is in scope.
[06:42] Marcus: On the technical path for private deployments, there is a checklist: network peering, KMS, NACLs, and instance sizing. We'll include the diagram. Some terms like K-V cache in our runtime may be transcribed as K-V cash in auto transcript -- apologies.
[06:56] Priya: Is there a limit to how many seats/engineers we can add during the pilot?
[07:02] Lena: No strict limit for pilot access—just let us know who needs console access and we'll add RBAC roles.
[07:09] Sanjay: For benchmarking we need to capture GPU utilization metrics and host-level metrics; do you provide exporters?
[07:16] Marcus: Yes, we provide Prometheus metrics and logs; we'll share dashboards.
[07:20] Tom: Let's nail down timeline: start pilot week of Oct 6, 2025, four weeks of active testing, final review week of Nov 3. Is that feasible?
[07:29] Lena: Yes, that timeline works. We'll aim to have the POC doc and credit proposal to you by Oct 3.
[07:33] Megan: We'll need a PO or contract signature by Nov 30 ideally.
[07:37] Lena: Noted.
[07:40] Ana: About benchmarks—what models will you run? Can we test multiple model families?
[07:45] Marcus: Yeah we can test a couple of compatible model variants—smaller quantized ones for latency, and larger for quality. We'll recommend model/quantization profiles.
[07:54] Priya: Any known caveats with quantization and clinical text?
[07:58] Marcus: Sometimes quantization slightly impacts tokenization-sensitive tasks; we'll watch for regression and recommend fallbacks.
[08:06] Tom: Procurement question—what's included in the pilot support? Dedicated AE/SE time?
[08:11] Lena: Included: weekly syncs, access to SE for troubleshooting (up to X hours), and a post-pilot wrap with recommended production config. Extra professional services can be quoted.
[08:21] Priya: Ok, let's summarize success criteria and commercial guardrails.
[08:24] Lena: Summing up: 4-week pilot (start week Oct 6), $25k credits or fixed-fee option, success criteria spreadsheet to include p95 latency thresholds, <=5% regression on quality metrics, cost per 1k tokens within 20% of baseline, and a clear procurement path with MSA/SOC2/BAA provided. If credits are exhausted we can either allow overage at agreed rate or pause the pilot—will include caps.
[08:52] Priya: Good. Please include an explicit clause for PHI handling and proof of KMS support.
[08:58] Lena: Will do.
[09:01] Marcus: I'll share the benchmark plan and sample scripts.
[09:04] Megan: We'll review and revert with procurement checklist.
[09:07] Lena: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the POC doc and next steps.

Action / Next steps (recap): Lena to send the POC commercial guardrails and credit proposal; Marcus to share benchmark template and cluster sizing worksheet; Zenith to provide prompt set and infra profile; schedule deep dive with infra.

Transcript notes: occasional auto-transcription mistakes (K-V cash vs KV cache, Redwood product names sometimes truncated). Speakers occasionally labeled generically in auto transcript; final export has been lightly cleaned for readability.
